development: AI research assistants for literature discovery and synthesis
definition: LLM-based tools that search large paper corpora, summarise findings and extract structured evidence tables from natural-language research questions.
named_examples: Elicit (Elicit; S019, b8-007); Consensus (Consensus.app; b8-007); Undermind; Scopus AI via EKUAL/EBSCO-type licences (b8-011, b8-012)
leader_status: Scaled commercial use in US/EU; independent tests find Elicit search sensitivity ~39.5% vs 94.5% for conventional searching, so adjunct only (b8-007, S019).
analogue_status: Brazil: CAPES supplies Elsevier LeapSpace AI search to national institutions (b8-013, secondary report). Poland, Mexico, Indonesia, South Korea: not sourced.
tr_status: pilot: EKUAL national licence and EBSCO AI-search trainings (b8-011, b8-012); 515 Turkish academics report generative-AI literature-review use (b8-001). No Elicit/Consensus deployment found.

development: LLM-assisted screening and data extraction in systematic reviews
definition: Human-in-the-loop use of LLMs for title/abstract screening and data extraction, with reported workload reductions but variable accuracy on numerical outcomes.
named_examples: Elicit Systematic Review (Elicit; b8-008 F1 92% extraction); Claude 2 data extraction, 96.3% accuracy (Gartlehner et al., Research Synthesis Methods; S014); GPT-4 prompt templates, sensitivity 97.7% (Cao et al., Annals of Internal Medicine; b8-003)
leader_status: Growing, mostly academic validation: 63-study review gives median screening agreement 0.92/0.89, extraction accuracy median 0.95 but 0.36-1.00; cautious implementation advised (S017).
analogue_status: No in-country application in Poland, Brazil, Mexico, Indonesia or South Korea sourced (author affiliations not visible in abstracts). Analogue count 0 is an unsourced gap, not evidence of absence.
tr_status: absent: no Turkish LLM-screening study or deployment found (EN search incl. Turkiye terms; no TR-language search possible); generic GenAI literature-review use among Turkish academics (b8-001).
class_branch: 1-2y: C1 fail (d1 2<4, d6 2<4, funded no) -> C2 fail (barrier none, min(d4,d5) 3>1, mean 3.5>=2.0) -> C3 fail (d3 4>=4 but analogues 0<2) -> C4 Potential; 3-5y: no dated obligation, d6 unchanged (analogues 0<2), same chain -> C4 Potential
deciding_condition: Sourced in-country LLM-assisted screening/extraction by research groups in at least two analogue economies (with d3=4 this would give Likely).
notes: Anchor DOI 10.1016/j.jclinepi.2026.112221 (Laignelot et al. 2026, J Clin Epidemiol) confirmed in a Consensus search result; kept (S017). d3 4: sourced screening workload cuts 33-93% (b8-004), 65-85% simulated (b8-005), cost USD 157 vs >USD 1,667 per 10,000 citations (b8-003); retrospective/simulated and extraction less reliable (b8-006 outcome no-error 27.8-80.7%; b8-044 moderate), so not 5. d4 4: API cost USD 0.14-1.93 per review (b8-009). d5 3: zero-shot sensitivity 49% vs 97.7% with tuned prompts (b8-003). d2 2: unsourced estimate, EU/TUBITAK funding not searched specifically. d6 2: only generic survey signal (b8-001). near-Likely trigger NOT applied (analogues 0), but analogue evidence is likely under-detected; recommend targeted check (BR/KR/PL groups). Horizon adjustment none. Confidence med-low.

development: AI-maintained living evidence databases for conservation decisions
definition: LLM pipelines that screen and classify conservation literature and answer questions on intervention effectiveness from curated evidence databases.
named_examples: Conservation Evidence (University of Cambridge; b8-030, b8-031); Imperial College London AI evidence pipeline (Alec Christie; S047); Iyer et al. LLM pipeline on Conservation Evidence database (PLOS One 2025; b8-029)
leader_status: UK pilot/growing: Evidence Pipeline screened ~250 million papers (b8-031); LLM pipelines matched human experts on 45 filtered questions (b8-029). No EU/US/China deployment sourced.
analogue_status: No analogue deployment sourced. A Spanish-language screening classifier exists but is not an analogue-country deployment; Poland, Brazil, Mexico, Indonesia, South Korea unsourced.
tr_status: absent: no Turkish AI-maintained evidence database found; Turkish biodiversity programmes (Biodiversa+ via TUBITAK) exist but are not evidence-synthesis pipelines (calib-049).
class_branch: 1-2y: C1 fail (d1 2<4, d6 2<4, funded no) -> C2 fail (barrier none, min(d4,d5) 3>1, mean 3.0>=2.0) -> C3 fail (d2 3<4, d3 3<4; analogues 0<2) -> C4 Potential; 3-5y: no dated obligation, d6 unchanged, same chain -> C4 Potential

tr_status: absent: no Turkish institutional use of agentic coding tools found; only generic GenAI use for data analysis among 515 academics (b8-001).

development: Publisher, funder and university rules on generative AI in research (authoring, peer review, grant applications)
definition: Governance policies from publishers, funders and universities restricting or conditioning use of generative AI in research, peer review and applications.
named_examples: Elsevier generative AI policy for journals (S039); Springer Nature reviewer guidance (b8-018); NIH NOT-OD-23-149 (b8-019); YOK Etik Rehberi on generative AI in research (b8-014)
leader_status: Scaled: Elsevier and Springer Nature bar uploading manuscripts to AI tools in review; NIH prohibits AI use by reviewers; ERA Living Guidelines revised May 2026 (S039, b8-018, b8-019, S044).
analogue_status: Poland NCN position May 2025 (b8-021); Brazil CNPq Ordinance 2.664/2026 (b8-022, secondary); South Korea NRF/MoE guide (b8-023, secondary). Indonesia guide is learning-focused, not counted (b8-024).
tr_status: exists: YOK ethics guide approved 18 Apr 2024 and sent to universities (b8-014); university guides (b8-015, b8-016); TUBITAK funder rule (calib-041); journal AI policies (b8-017).
